question: Does the real interactive Web contain predictive structure BEYOND memory and ordinary similarity, tested at the coarsest level of description and on real sites rather than on synthetic data-generating processes? Using a frozen, preregistered pool of real credential-free public origins (disjoint from the graph and frontier host sets this cycle), with state represented as a response signature over (status, selected header fields, body-shape summary) and actions as the frozen GET-path transformations available without credentials: does an INHERITED-MECHANISM predictor — conditioning on a mechanism's declared semantic effect and its BOUND parameter values, as SPIDER's product would actually condition on — predict the held-out response signature of a NEVER-OBSERVED identifier better than (B1) a first-order Markov model on (URL, action), (B2) TF-IDF k5 retrieval over the training responses, and (B3) cold re-derivation with no stored knowledge, scored by held-out log predictive density and Brier score on the response signature, with trajectory- and site-grouped permutation nulls and site-clustered intervals?
hypothesis: An inherited-mechanism predictor that conditions on a mechanism's declared semantic effect and its bound parameter values will achieve higher held-out log predictive density and lower Brier score on response signatures of never-observed identifiers than all three baselines (first-order Markov, TF-IDF k5 retrieval, cold re-derivation), demonstrating predictive structure beyond memory and ordinary similarity on real credential-free public Web origins.
falsifier: The inherited-mechanism predictor does not outperform all three baselines on both held-out log predictive density and Brier score, or the improvement is not statistically distinguishable from the trajectory- and site-grouped permutation nulls, or the positive control (planted mechanism) is not detected, or the placebo control (permuted mechanism) is spuriously detected.

baselines.description: First-order Markov model on (URL, action) predicting response signature. Trained on observed transitions, predicts held-out response signature for never-observed identifiers via empirical conditional distribution P(response_signature | URL, action).
baselines.expected_behavior: Captures memory-based predictability from exact (URL, action) pairs observed in training. Should not generalize to never-observed identifiers.

baselines.description: TF-IDF k=5 retrieval over training response signatures. For a held-out query, retrieves 5 nearest training responses by cosine similarity on TF-IDF vectors of (URL, action, response_signature) and averages their response signatures.
baselines.expected_behavior: Captures ordinary similarity-based predictability. Should not generalize to never-observed identifiers beyond lexical/structural similarity.

baselines.description: Cold re-derivation with no stored knowledge. Predicts the marginal distribution of response signatures observed in training, ignoring the query entirely.
baselines.expected_behavior: Represents the no-knowledge floor. Any predictor must beat this to demonstrate positive knowledge value.

positive_control.description: A planted mechanism whose declared semantic effect and bound parameter values are known by construction to determine the response signature. The mechanism is inserted into the mechanism pool with a unique identifier never observed in training. The response signature for its identifier is generated by a known deterministic function of the bound parameters. The predictor must detect this mechanism and achieve near-perfect prediction on its held-out identifiers.
positive_control.expected_behavior: Must be detected (high log predictive density, low Brier score). Demonstrates the accept branch is reachable before freeze.
positive_control.construction: Mechanism 'PLANTED_DETERMINISTIC_ECHO' with semantic effect 'echoes bound parameter in response body shape', parameter 'echo_value' bound to a known string. Response signature body_shape_summary includes the echo_value. Training data contains transitions for other identifiers; held-out test contains only the planted mechanism's never-observed identifier.

null_control.description: The identical inherited-mechanism predictor architecture, but conditioned on a mechanism whose declaration and parameter values are randomly permuted across all mechanisms in the pool. This null must be a different object from the statistic (not a relabeling of the treatment labels), as the count-preserving relabeling null in the parent packet had provably zero power against label-readers. A genuine mechanism reader must FAIL to detect this placebo; a label-only reader must detect it.
null_control.expected_behavior: Must NOT outperform baselines. A genuine mechanism-reading predictor should fail to reject this null. If it spuriously outperforms baselines, the predictor is reading labels/structure not mechanism semantics.

null_control.description: A response-signature process generated i.i.d. within each site (preserving marginal distribution of response signatures per site but destroying all sequential and cross-identifier structure). The predictor runs on this i.i.d. process and must return no structure (performance at or below cold re-derivation baseline).
null_control.expected_behavior: Must return no predictive structure beyond marginal baseline. Validates that the measurement apparatus does not hallucinate structure in pure noise.

measurement_validity: TARGET INTEGRITY: The inherited-mechanism predictor's features (mechanism declaration, bound parameters) are constructed solely from training data. The held-out test identifiers are never observed during training. No predictor contains the target response signature directly or deterministically.

SPLIT INTEGRITY: Holdout is at the identifier level (never-observed identifiers), not transition level. Site identity is explicit in the grouping for clustered intervals but does not leak into the predictor's features for never-observed identifiers. Preprocessing (TF-IDF vocabulary, response signature schema) is fit on TRAIN only.

SAMPLING INTEGRITY: Seeds are deterministic and recorded. The predictor's policy (which mechanism to apply) is explicitly described and separated from the environment dynamics (response signature generation). The pool of real origins is frozen and preregistered before any measurement.

UNCERTAINTY INTEGRITY: Resampling unit matches dependency structure: trajectory-grouped and site-grouped permutation nulls; site-clustered confidence intervals. Correlated transitions within a trajectory/site are not treated as independent. No arbitrary injected noise.

REPRESENTATION INTEGRITY: Raw HTTP responses (status, headers, body) are preserved. Response signature is a lossy but operationally defined summary. Representation losses (body -> body-shape-summary) are documented. The predictor operates on the same representation as baselines.

decision_rule.significance_threshold: p < 0.05 under trajectory- and site-grouped permutation nulls for both metrics simultaneously
decision_rule.acceptance_criterion: The inherited-mechanism predictor must outperform ALL three baselines (B1, B2, B3) on BOTH metrics, with site-clustered confidence intervals excluding zero improvement, AND the positive control must be detected (log predictive density > threshold derived from power calculation), AND the placebo control must NOT be detected (performance not significantly above baselines), AND the i.i.d. null must return no structure.
decision_rule.power_calculation: Pre-freeze power calculation based on pilot data from the frozen origin pool: minimum detectable effect size for log predictive density improvement over best baseline, with alpha=0.05, power=0.8, using site-clustered bootstrap. Recorded in prereg.md with real values.
decision_rule.site_clustered_intervals: Confidence intervals for metric differences computed by site-clustered bootstrap (1000 resamples of sites, not transitions), respecting within-site correlation.

product_consequence_positive: Physics establishes that real credential-free Web contains predictive dynamical structure beyond memory/similarity at the mechanism level. This opens the physics program on real data for the first time, enabling downstream work on effect factorization, barriers, timescales, geometry, or multiscale dynamics on real Web transitions. Product can consider mechanism-level priors for exploration.
product_consequence_negative: Physics obtains its first genuinely informative negative on C-WEB-DYNAMICS with a site-clustered interval whose lower bound sits at or below zero. This correctly redirects the physics lane away from single-agent P(S'|S,A) on this data class (credential-free public HTTP with response-signature representation). The lane must pivot to orthogonal mechanisms (effect factorization, barriers, timescales, geometry, multiscale) or other data classes.
expected_information_gain: High. This is the first Physics experiment on real Web data with honest nulls (first-order Markov, TF-IDF retrieval) that directly test the claim's actual question (predictive structure beyond memory/similarity) at the mechanism level where SPIDER's product operates. A positive opens the real-Web physics program; a negative with valid interval is the first decision-quality negative in this lane's history.
